item.title: DSPy-Go brings systematic prompt engineering to Go applications
item.description:
DSPy-Go brings systematic prompt engineering to Go applications

DSPy-Go is a native Go implementation of the DSPy framework, bringing systematic prompt engineering and automated reasoning capabilities to Go applications. It enables developers to build reliable LLM applications through composable modules and workflows.

🧩 How it works

DSPy-Go supports various reasoning patterns and optimization techniques:

  • Predict, ChainOfThought, ReAct, RLM, Refine, and Parallel modules
  • ReAct patterns and the ACE framework for self-improving agents
  • Multi-agent orchestration with hierarchical composition
  • Bayesian selection, chaining, composition, and MCP integration
  • GEPA, MIPRO, SIMBA, BootstrapFewShot, and COPRO optimizers

The framework includes JSON structured output and XML adapters with security controls.

⚙️ Key details

Key technical features include:

  • Support for Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, Ollama, LlamaCPP, and more
  • Model resolution order: module-local via SetLLM, request-local via core.WithRuntime, then package default configured with core.SetDefaultLLM
  • Helper functions such as core.SetDefaultLLM, core.SetTeacherLLM, and core.GetConcurrencyLevel are preferred over mutating core.GlobalConfig directly
  • Signatures can be defined with input/output fields and instructions, such as answering questions concisely
  • Interceptors for XML configuration, such as interceptors.ApplyXMLInterceptors
  • Keyless web search and page fetch through MCP
  • Comparison of full, checkpointed, and adaptive replay modes
Module Function
Predict Direct prediction
ChainOfThought Step-by-step reasoning
ReAct Reasoning + tool use
RLM Large context exploration via REPL
Refine Quality improvement through iteration
Parallel Concurrent batch processing

🚀 Availability

DSPy-Go is available via:

  • go get github.com/XiaoConstantine/dspy-go
  • CLI tools: ./dspy-cli try mipro –dataset gsm8k to test optimizer instantly; ./dspy-cli view session.jsonl –stats to view RLM session logs
  • API key setup: export GEMINI_API_KEY=“your-api-key”
  • Instantiating LLMs: llm, err := llms.NewGeminiLLM("", core.ModelGoogleGeminiPro)

#DSPy #Go #LLM #PromptEngineering #AI

Source: XiaoConstantine/dspy-go

item.title: DSPy adds Monty Python interpreter for secure code execution
item.description:
DSPy adds Monty Python interpreter for secure code execution

A new drop-in code interpreter for DSPy’s Reasoning Language Model (RLM) module utilizes Monty, a secure Python interpreter written in Rust. This integration allows AI-generated code to run in a sandboxed environment, serving as a daily driver for many RLM use cases due to its speed.

#DSPy #Python #AI #Sandbox #RLM

item.title: MIT CSAIL Introduces RLM for Interpretable, Adaptive AI Workflows
item.description:
MIT CSAIL Introduces RLM for Interpretable, Adaptive AI Workflows

Researchers at MIT CSAIL have released predict-rlm, a production-focused runtime that lets language models execute complex, adaptive workflows while maintaining full interpretability. Built on the Recursive Language Models paper by Alex L. Zhang, Tim Kranca, and Omar Khattab, the system enables models to call sub-LMs with DSPy signatures, inspect files, manage state, and handle large contexts through code — all without context rot or loss of control flow visibility.

#AI #ML #LLM #MITCSAIL #DSPy #predict-rlm

Source: avalanche-run/predict-rlm

item.title: Stanford releases DSPy: Declarative Python framework for programming language models
item.description:
Stanford releases DSPy: Declarative Python framework for programming language models

The Stanford NLP group announced DSPy, a new Python framework that lets developers program language models directly rather than rely on brittle prompts.

🔍 Overview

  • DSPy is the framework for programming—rather than prompting—language models.
  • DSPy stands for Declarative Self-improving Python.

🧩 How it works

  • Instead of brittle prompts, you write compositional Python code and use DSPy to teach your LM to deliver high-quality outputs.
  • It lets you iterate fast on building modular AI systems and provides algorithms for optimizing prompts and weights, suitable for simple classifiers, sophisticated RAG pipelines, or Agent loops.

⚙️ Key details

  • The current LM integration uses bundled native lm15 engines, without a LiteLLM runtime dependency or fallback.
  • See the LM migration guide for breaking changes to provider options, custom LMs, text completions, and embeddings.

📚 Research timeline

Date Title
Jul'25 GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning
Jun'24 Optimizing Instructions and Demonstrations for Multi-Stage Language Model Programs
Oct'23 DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines
Jul'24 Fine-Tuning and Prompt Optimization: Two Great Steps that Work Better Together
Jun'24 Prompts as Auto-Optimized Training Hyperparameters
Feb'24 Assisting in Writing Wikipedia-like Articles From Scratch with Large Language Models
Jan'24 In-Context Learning for Extreme Multi-Label Classification
Dec'23 DSPy Assertions: Computational Constraints for Self-Refining Language Model Pipelines
Dec'22 Demonstrate-Search-Predict: Composing Retrieval & Language Models for Knowledge-Intensive NLP

🚀 Availability

  • Install via pip: pip install dspy
  • Install latest from source: pip install git+https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy.git

🎨 Branding

  • The DSPy logo is designed by Chuyi Zhang.

item.title: DSPyGen Offers a Rails-Inspired CLI for Building DSPy Modules
item.description:
DSPyGen Offers a Rails-Inspired CLI for Building DSPy Modules

DSPyGen is a command-line framework for developing language-model pipelines with DSPy, using a structured, modular approach inspired by Ruby on Rails.

🔍 Overview

DSPyGen is described as a framework for the DSPy project, which works with language models such as GPT, BERT, and Llama. Its stated aim is to simplify creating, developing, and deploying LM pipelines. The project says it was influenced by the work of Sean Chatman and James I. Chatman.

🧩 How it works

The CLI provides commands to initialize a project, generate DSPy modules, run a module, and serve a REST API:

1
2
3
4
5
6
7

dspygen init my_project
cd my_project

dspygen module new -cn TextSummarizer -i "text" -o "summary"
dspygen module text_summarizer call "Gettysburg address"

docker-compose up app

The dspygen module new command creates modules. Its listed options are:

  • --class-name, -cn: required module class name.
  • --inputs, -i: comma-separated input names.
  • --output, -o: output name.
  • --help: show command help and exit.

⚙️ Example modules

Example Inputs Output
Text summarization text summary
Sentiment analysis text sentiment
YouTube comment generation vid_title,words viral_comment
Machine translation source_text,target_language translated_text
Code generation prompt generated_code

The project also says it generates a mocked pytest module for provided Python source code.

🚀 Model setup examples

The examples show initializing DSPy with OpenAI and Groq, and initializing Ollama with init_ol:

  • OpenAI: init_dspy(model="gpt-4o", max_tokens=500)
  • Groq: The instructions say to obtain an API key from Groq and modify .env as demonstrated in .envDemo; the example uses init_dspy(model="llama3-70b-8192", lm_class=Groq, max_tokens=8000).
  • Ollama: The instructions say to install Ollama, then show init_ol(model="llama3", max_tokens=2000) followed by a call to the text summarizer module.
